title: Magnetoresistive Memory in the Paramagnetic Phase of Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$
authors: Sudhaman R. Balguri, Mira B. Mahendru, Rourav Basak, Enrique O. González-Delgado, Adam A. Aczel, David E. Graf, Andreas Rydh, Christopher C. Homes, Jonathan Gaudet, Ying Ran, Alex Frano, Fazel Tafti
abstract: Magnetoresistive materials that respond sensitively to applied fields are central to modern data storage technologies. Here we unveil a novel Magnetoresistive Memory (MRM) in Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$, where the electrical resistivity depends not only on the magnitude but also on the history of the applied magnetic field. Such an effect has been reported in only two classes of strongly correlated electron systems: perovskite manganites and pyrochlore iridates. In both cases, the effect has been observed in the magnetically ordered phase. It has been attributed to metastable magnetic states in manganites and conducting domain walls in iridates. Remarkably, the MRM in Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ onsets at twice the antiferromagnetic transition temperature, well within the paramagnetic phase. The temperature, field, and time dependence of resistivity suggest that either a hidden order or a fluctuating phase with short-range correlations underlies this effect. Our results offer MRM as a new platform for quantum sensing and memory technologies, and encourage searching for MRM in related materials.
summary: This work reports discovering a Magnetoresistive Memory (MRM) effect in Eu5In2As6 that persists deep within the paramagnetic phase, unlike previously studied materials. The persistence of this history-dependent resistivity suggests an underlying mechanism rooted in short-range correlations or hidden order rather than long-range magnetic ordering. This establishes the material as a promising platform for quantum memory applications.
main_problem: The study investigates a novel Magnetoresistive Memory (MRM) effect in Eu5In2As6, particularly focusing on its persistence and mechanism within the paramagnetic phase.
main_result: The MRM effect is observed well into the paramagnetic regime, suggesting underlying physics related to short-range correlations or hidden order rather than simple magnetic domain wall dynamics seen in other materials.
method: Measurements include resistivity vs. applied field/temperature sweeps, time-dependent measurements, and X-ray diffraction analysis of lattice parameters.
model_or_system: The physical system is the semiconductor compound Eu5In2As6, a magnetic material exhibiting A-type AFM ordering at 16 K. The study compares its MRM behavior to known systems like manganites and iridates.
key_observables: Resistivity ($ho$) hysteresis loops (untrained vs. trained states), lattice parameter contraction along the c-axis, and temperature dependence of the memory effect.
important_parameters: The MRM onset temperature (~30 K in some analyses) is significantly above the AFM transition temperature ($T_N = 16 	ext{ K}$); carrier concentration plays a critical role.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that resistivity relaxation and lattice contraction are intrinsic to the material's electronic state, ruling out simple Joule heating effects.
figures_summary: Figures compare MRM across different magnetic materials; others show $ho(T)$ curves for trained/untrained samples, field dependence of hysteresis loops, and lattice parameter changes correlated with the MRM onset temperature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically establishes the existence of MRM in Eu5In2As6 above $T_N$, contrasts it with known magnetic ordering mechanisms, investigates its coupling to structural changes (lattice contraction), and finally uses symmetry analysis to constrain potential underlying physical models.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state magnetism, the investigation into history dependence, hidden order, and correlation between electronic transport and lattice structure touches upon non-equilibrium dynamics and emergent quantum states relevant to correlated electron physics.
